edits.headline: Kenya releases 20 Ebola contacts from quarantine after 21 days
edits.subheadline: Another 98 contacts of the country's first Ebola case remain in quarantine, UN News reported.
editorialBody: Twenty people who had been in contact with Kenya's first Ebola case were released from quarantine after 21 days of monitoring, UN News reported. Another 98 contacts remain in quarantine, it said.

Oil prices moved up and down as diplomatic efforts to end the conflict in the Middle East resumed, CNBC reported. Iran said the United States was not serious about talks, during a meeting in Tehran, Al Jazeera reported.
In the US, House Speaker Mike Johnson predicted that the Democrats' shift to the left would increase enthusiasm for Republicans in the midterm elections, Fox News reported.

Chinese President Xi Jinping congratulated Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on his re-election as president of Brazil, Xinhua reported. Pope Leo is keeping his November trip to South America after lung surgery, Bloomberg reported.

Russia's trade with South Africa is above $1 billion a year, TASS reported. In Johannesburg, homes belonging to the Gupta family have been put up for sale, and stigma attached to the family has reduced buyers' interest, Bloomberg reported.
Bloomberg reported that Anthropic was giving traders a pure-play bet on frontier AI. Commercial real estate debt is coming due, and CNBC reported that this presents a "massive" opportunity.
In the UK, two people have been charged with national security offences over an incident at RAF Fairford, BBC News reported.
